name: Trelleborg Engineered Coated Fabrics
old_description: Discover how our material engineering approach improves performance across multiple industries:
about:
Trelleborg Engineered Coated Fabrics operates from Rutherfordton, North Carolina, as a division of the global Trelleborg Group. The business traces its roots to 1905 when Henry Dunker founded Trelleborgs Gummifabriks AB in Sweden, initially producing bicycle and car tires, industrial rubber goods, and raincoats. Through a series of acquisitions — including Reeves Brothers in 2006, Uretek Archer in 2014, Dartex Holdings and Lamcotec in 2018, and the Fairprene and FluoroSeal operations from Alpha Engineered Composites in 2021 — the company has expanded its coated-fabric portfolio and North American footprint.

The company develops and manufactures custom polymer-coated fabrics using coating, lamination, and hot-melt technologies. Its product lines encompass Dartex medical fabrics, Fairprene diaphragm and gasket materials, FluoroSeal fluoroelastomer sheet packing, Pipecure trenchless pipe-rehabilitation liners, REEVECOTE sealing solutions, TACTWEAR flame-resistant defense textiles, and Vapex arc-resistant high-visibility fabrics. Trelleborg also supplies uncoated textiles and works with substrates ranging from knits to woven fabrics, pairing them with rubber, polyurethane, silicone, and fluoroelastomer coatings to meet specific performance requirements.

Customers span aerospace, automotive, safety and protection, healthcare and medical, outdoor and recreation, general manufacturing, marine, rail and mass transit, and defense sectors. Notable applications include aerostats for the National Missile Defense (JLENS) program, pressure-injury-prevention fabrics for hospitals, and Berry Amendment-compliant materials for military and law-enforcement personnel.

Trelleborg emphasizes over 100 years of manufacturing excellence and a material-engineering approach that combines process engineering and chemistry to accelerate performance sustainably. The company states that its relentless curiosity to understand customer applications drives innovation, while sustainability initiatives across its sites target carbon neutrality and environmental responsibility.

about:
Trendtex Fabrics & Tropical Paper Garden operates from Honolulu, Hawaii, offering a range of fabric collections sold by the yard. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company stocks 234 fabric products across categories including cotton poplin, rayon poplin, polyester kapena, polyester knit moana, TC blend, cotton dobby, canvas, twill, yarn-dyed palaka, and Hawaiian barkcloth upholstery fabric. Fabrics are sold by the full yard and packed as continuous yardage per item unless otherwise communicated.

The fabric selections serve apparel, upholstery, and home décor markets, with materials such as 100% cotton poplin for shirts and dresses, rayon poplin for lightweight garments, and barkcloth for furniture upholstery. Customers include designers, manufacturers, and retail buyers seeking Hawaiian-inspired textiles.

Trendtex emphasizes continuous-yardage packing and a broad in-stock assortment of Hawaiian-themed fabrics, positioning itself as a major supplier of barkcloth upholstery material in the region.

name: Trexon - Integrated Cable Systems (ICS)
old_description: A prominent manufacturer of Image Guided Therapy Devices needs cables with an exceptionally tight bend radius for their new laser product...
about:
Integrated Cable Systems (ICS) operates from Longmont, Colorado, as a supplier of specialized cable assemblies, wire harnesses, and electro-mechanical assemblies. The company holds ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certifications and describes itself as a turn-key provider with decades of technical and manufacturing engineering experience.

ICS manufactures custom cable assemblies and wire harnesses, including discrete wire harnesses, complex routed harnesses, jacketed cable assemblies, molded cable assemblies, jumper cable assemblies, and SCSI and RJ45 cable assemblies. Its capabilities extend to MS connector and crimping applications, engineering consultation, development of customer documentation, and testing of custom interconnect products. The facility uses a Schleuniger PowerStrip 9580 automatic cut-and-strip machine for wires up to 70 mm² (2/0 AWG), shielded cables, and complex multiconductor applications, supporting cutting, stripping, and marking operations.

The company serves aerospace, defense, and medical industries. A noted project involved a manufacturer of image-guided therapy devices requiring cables with an exceptionally tight bend radius for a new laser product, delivered in partnership with Cicoil for high-flex flat cable and custom molded panel grommets.

ICS emphasizes its focus on high-cost-of-failure applications, combining deep expertise, relentless innovation, and customer focus to solve complex connectivity challenges. The company states its purpose is to deliver innovative connectivity solutions with uncompromising quality and continuous improvement.

about:
Tri W-G Inc. has been manufacturing physical therapy and rehabilitation equipment in Valley City, North Dakota, since 1967. Founded as a medical device maker, the company remains at its original location on 12th Avenue NE, where it produces a range of devices designed for clinical durability.

The product line includes parallel bars, mat tables, treatment tables, trainer tables, and tilt tables, along with a bariatric series that supports weight capacities up to 1,000 pounds. Each unit carries a UL Classified safety label earned through independent testing, and the bariatric models are backed by a 10‑year limited warranty.

Tri W-G serves hospitals, outpatient clinics, rehabilitation centers, and architects specifying equipment for healthcare facilities. Its devices are used in physical therapy, bariatric care, and hospital architecture design, with some early units still in service decades after installation.

The company emphasizes long‑term reliability and risk reduction, building every product to meet stringent safety standards so that clinicians can focus on patient care rather than equipment failure.

name: Triad Fastener LP
old_description: We are always looking for talented individuals to join our company. Check out our open positions.
about:
Triad Fastener LP operates from Alda, Nebraska, a location just off Interstate 80 that the company says provides reliable transportation and a steady labor pool for its Midwest customer base. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company runs a clean, modern facility housing 19 injection molding machines with clamp capacities from 60 to 650 tons. Its core processes include two-shot molding, gas-assist molding, two-color molding, horizontal insert molding, and elastomeric over-molding. In-house capabilities extend to mold design, service, and repair; a quality lab with CMM documentation; rapid prototyping via fused deposition modeling and soft tooling; and secondary operations such as machining, assembly, sonic welding, pad printing, hot stamping, specialty packaging, and kitting. Automated assembly and inspection cells support production consistency.

Triad Fastener serves customers across the Midwest with custom injection molding services and also markets proprietary product lines, notably the DamGates® brand, through its sister company Triad Products. Specific industry sectors are not detailed in public materials.

The company emphasizes its practice of Scientific Molding principles to establish robust, repeatable processes that minimize cost and quality issues. It also highlights ongoing automation investments to reduce labor costs and improve process consistency, positioning these approaches as key differentiators.

name: Tricol Biomedical, Inc.
old_description: Tricol Is Focused On Saving Lives Through Innovation In Hemostasis.
about:
Tricol Biomedical, Inc. is headquartered in Portland, Oregon, where it was established in 2001 as a U.S. corporation. The company originated from battlefield needs, partnering with the U.S. Army to create the first advanced hemostatic dressing for soldiers suffering traumatic injuries.

The company develops, manufactures, and markets a range of hemostatic and wound-care products built on its proprietary chitosan technology, branded as Chito+. Its product lines include HemCon® dressings for trauma management, OneStop™ devices for procedural care, and ChitoGauze® bandages for consumer self-care. Tricol operates as a fully integrated medical device company, handling research, development, and production in-house.

Tricol serves military, pre-hospital, and hospital markets, with documented use by U.S. Special Operations forces, emergency physicians, dialysis centers, oral surgeons, and general consumers. The HemCon bandage has been deployed in combat zones since 2003 and is also used in civilian settings such as cardiac surgery, vascular procedures, and home first aid.

The company's stated vision is to achieve zero preventable deaths due to blood loss. Founded on the premise of saving and improving lives, Tricol's mission centers on innovation in hemostasis, driven by its battlefield origins and a commitment to advancing the standard of care in bleeding control.

about:
Tropical Assemblies Inc operates from a facility at 4066 NE 5th Avenue in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. The company’s founding year and ownership structure have not been disclosed publicly.

The company provides electronic manufacturing services (EMS) with a focus on high-complexity, high-reliability assemblies. Its capabilities span printed circuit board assembly, electro-mechanical integration, RF and high-frequency communications hardware, LED lighting electronics, and full box-build services. Tropical Assemblies also offers design support covering hardware, firmware, and mechanical engineering, along with supply chain management. The firm describes its operation as a "Smart Technology Factory" with real-time data tracking and audited quality systems.

Tropical Assemblies serves the aerospace, defense, medical, communications, LED lighting, and industrial controls sectors. In aerospace, it produces electronics for commercial and military programs worldwide. For defense, it supplies circuit board and electro-mechanical assemblies to armed forces. Its medical work, compliant with ISO 13485, supports device pioneers globally. The communications practice specializes in RF/HF systems, while the industrial controls group brings combined hardware, software, and mechanical design to market.

The company highlights its recognition as a finalist for the South Florida Manufacturers Association’s 2020 Manufacturer of the Year award and emphasizes its certified quality standards—AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, ITAR registration, and UL certification—as core differentiators.

Tru Fru operates from Salt Lake City, Utah. Public sources do not disclose the company's founding year, ownership structure, or the names of its founders.

The company manufactures two distinct product lines: Hyper-Chilled, featuring frozen fresh fruit enrobed in chocolate, and Hyper-Dried, featuring freeze-dried fruit enrobed in chocolate. The assortment spans strawberries, raspberries, bananas, blueberries, cherries, and pineapple, with coatings that include dark chocolate, milk chocolate, white chocolate, and combinations such as dark and white or milk and white. Several SKUs incorporate Greek yogurt, granola, peanut butter, coconut, or a crème layer. The company does not publish facility square footage, employee headcount, or annual production volumes.

Distribution reaches consumers through the company's e-commerce site and through brick-and-mortar retail. Customer testimonials on the site reference purchases at Costco and at Walmart checkout displays, suggesting placement in warehouse clubs and mass-market grocery chains.

Marketing materials highlight simple ingredient lists and a positioning as a better-for-you sweet snack, with reviewers commenting on the nutritional facts relative to conventional chocolate-dipped fruit. name: Trusted Semiconductor Solutions
old_description: Microelectronics development from concept to qualified part delivery
about:
Semiconductor Solutions was founded in 2006 and is based in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota. The company operates as a small business concern and non‑traditional defense contractor with DoD Category 1A Accreditation. No individual founders are named in the public materials.

The firm functions as a fabless semiconductor design and product development house, specializing in radiation‑hardened microelectronics. Its service portfolio covers analog/mixed‑signal and ASIC/SoC design, semiconductor IP development, chiplet and high‑density package design, wafer foundry coordination, package assembly, test and screening, printed circuit board design, and procurement services. The engineering staff includes IC design and verification engineers, analog/mixed‑signal/digital IP designers, package designers, board designers, and system engineers. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

Semiconductor Solutions serves aerospace, defense, industrial, medical, avionics, military, and space markets. Its microelectronics enable next‑generation systems as well as sustainment of mission‑critical platforms, including legacy part replacement for obsolete commercial‑off‑the‑shelf components.

The company differentiates itself through its fabless model, which provides access to state‑of‑the‑practice (45 nm and above) and state‑of‑the‑art (sub‑28 nm) foundry technologies such as CMOS, SOI, FinFET, SiGe, BiCMOS, bipolar, and gate‑all‑around processes. It positions itself as a single point of contact from design through delivery, offering program management, consulting, and customer service.
